slides.title:
5 SEO
checks for
AI content
slides.accentLine: Google now calls it critical to fact-check AI content before publishing.

slides.title: Fact-check
slides.body: Google says AI output can contain inaccuracies, also known as hallucinations.
slides.action: Check every name, number and date against a source before you publish.
slides.example: An AI draft says a feature launched in 2024. The source says 2025.

slides.title: Review your
slides.body: Google's review rule covers title elements too, because they can appear in search results.
slides.action: Read each AI-written title. Does it promise what the page delivers?
slides.example: “Best prices in town” on a page without a single price.

slides.title: Check meta
slides.body: Meta descriptions are named in Google's update. They can show up as your search snippet.
slides.action: Compare each AI description with the page and fix anything it invents.
slides.example: “Free shipping worldwide” when the store only ships to 3 countries.

slides.title: Verify
slides.body: Structured data and image alt text are on Google's review list as well.
slides.action: Match schema prices, ratings and dates to the page. Read the alt text.
slides.example: JSON-LD says 4.9 stars, but the page shows no reviews at all.

slides.title: Add value,
slides.body: Google's spam policy: many AI pages without added value can be scaled content abuse.
slides.action: Before you publish, add something only you know: photos, data, experience.
slides.example: 100 near-identical city pages vs. 10 with real local details.

slides.title: Five checks,
slides.seed: An AI can draft it. A human should check it.
